title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: This diff does not introduce any SQL queries or raw SQL construction. All database operations use Django ORM (e.g., Stream.objects.create(), stream.refresh_from_db()), which inherently use parameterized queries. The test file also uses only ORM operations.

The diff adds comprehensive authorization checks to all stream management endpoints (GET, PATCH, PUT, DELETE, verify, status operations). Each endpoint now explicitly checks `request.user.has_perm('authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream', self.provider)` and raises PermissionDenied if the user lacks permission. This addresses CWE-862 (missing authorization on protected operations). The test file confirms these checks work correctly by verifying that unauthorized users receive 403 responses.

evidence.content:
res = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "authentik_providers_ssf:stream",
                kwargs={"application_slug": self.application.slug},
            ),
            HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f"Bearer {self.token.token}",
        )
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 403)
